title: Indian-Origin Couple Gives $20 Million to Create AI College at UNT
excerpt: Anuradha and Vikas Sinha's gift to the University of North Texas will establish the Anuradha and Vikas Sinha College of Artificial Intelligence and Advanced Analytics — the couple's third major investment in the university that educated them.
body:
• Anuradha and Vikas Sinha, who immigrated to the United States from India, have donated $20 million to the University of North Texas to establish a college devoted to artificial intelligence and advanced analytics.
  • The university will name the new school the Anuradha and Vikas Sinha College of Artificial Intelligence and Advanced Analytics, organized around two academic divisions and a new Applied AI and Data Science Institute.
  • The gift will fund six permanent endowments covering student scholarships, endowed professorships, college leadership, entrepreneurship, advanced research, and emerging technologies.
  • It is the couple's third major commitment to UNT, following a $3 million gift in 2024 to establish the Department of Data Science and $2.15 million for the Sinha Innovation Lab for Data Science.

DENTON, Texas — An Indian-origin couple has donated $20 million to the University of North Texas, the university announced Tuesday, to create a new college dedicated to artificial intelligence and advanced analytics that will carry their names. The gift ranks among the largest philanthropic commitments in UNT's history.

The new school will be called the Anuradha and Vikas Sinha College of Artificial Intelligence and Advanced Analytics. It will serve as an academic and research hub focused on intelligent systems, data analytics, cybersecurity, health informatics, and learning technologies, according to the university.

A gift years in the making

The $20 million commitment is not the Sinhas' first investment in UNT — it caps a relationship that has deepened over several years. In 2024, the couple gave $3 million to establish the Anuradha and Vikas Sinha Department of Data Science. A year later, they funded the Sinha Innovation Lab for Data Science with a $2.15 million gift.

Vikas Sinha earned his Ph.D. in information science from UNT in 2023 and now serves as vice president of the Mainframe Software Division at Broadcom. Both he and Anuradha Sinha earned bachelor's degrees in civil engineering from Sri Venkateswara University in India before moving to the United States, where they completed graduate degrees at Florida Atlantic University.

What the college will do

The college will bring together programs spanning artificial intelligence, cybersecurity, data science, advanced data analytics, health informatics, information science, library science, and learning technologies. Its academic programs will be organized into two complementary divisions.

The Division of Applied Intelligence and Informatics will focus on building and deploying intelligent systems — work in AI, cybersecurity, data science, advanced analytics, and health informatics. The Division of Information and Learning Applications will study how information and intelligent systems operate within human and institutional settings, covering information science, library science, and learning technologies.

It will also house a new Applied Artificial Intelligence and Data Science Institute, connecting AI and analytics research and education across the university to spur interdisciplinary research, shared infrastructure, and industry partnerships.

"It will prepare them to build it, understand it, question it, govern it and apply it responsibly — developing both the builders and the stewards of intelligent systems."

— Vikas Sinha, donor and Broadcom vice president

The gift aligns with UNT's "Look North: UNT 2030" strategic plan, which aims to reshape how the university prepares students for a changing labor market and accelerate interdisciplinary research.

The immigrant story behind the gift

The Sinhas' philanthropy carries a direct link to their own path as international students. Vikas Sinha said he arrived in America on a funded assistantship — someone investing in him before they knew what he might accomplish — and that the experience has shaped the couple's giving.

"Education changed the trajectory of my life," he said. "For us, this gift is about paying that opportunity forward and recognizing that immigrants don't simply participate in the American dream — they help build it."

UNT President Harrison Keller said the couple's story illustrates the broader contribution of international students to the United States. "They contribute ideas, build companies, create jobs, lead communities, and create opportunities for the generations who follow them," Keller said.

"International students come to our universities to learn, but their impact extends far beyond the degrees they earn. They contribute ideas, build companies, create jobs, lead communities, and create opportunities for the generations who follow them."

— Harrison Keller, UNT President

The couple's son, Suraj, has been part of the family's philanthropic journey at UNT — a family legacy that, as university officials noted, traces from one generation in Hyderabad to another in the United States.

What's next

UNT plans to hold a campus celebration honoring the naming of the new college later this year, bringing together the Sinha family, students, faculty, and the North Texas community. Vikas Sinha framed the timing as deliberate: "This was the right time to create the first college of artificial intelligence in North Texas because it's a transforming industry. Establishing the college of artificial intelligence now puts UNT at the forefront of thought leadership."
